The Partner Enablement Operations Manager is a senior operator and builder responsible for designing and running a scalable, predictable, and data-driven operating model for partner enablement at Databricks.

This role serves as the operational backbone and strategic integrator for partner enablement, connecting global strategy to regional execution across AMER, EMEA, and APJ regions while ensuring programs are delivered consistently, efficiently, and at scale.

The ideal candidate brings strong executive presence, systems thinking, and a bias for automation. They know how to reduce operational friction, build governance that scales, and introduce AI-enabled workflows that improve responsiveness without adding unnecessary complexity or headcount.

We are looking for A builder who can architect operating systems, drive cross-functional alignment, and convert recurring operational friction into structural improvement.

What You’ll Do

Own the partner enablement operating model, including core planning cadences, governance mechanisms, and execution frameworks that connect strategy to execution.

Run QBRs, MBRs, and executive reviews for partner enablement leadership, using clear metrics and forward-looking insights to drive accountability and decision-making.

Lead end-to-end execution of partner enablement initiatives, ensuring timelines, dependencies, and deliverables are managed effectively across functions and regions.

Build and maintain dashboards and operating reviews that surface partner engagement, program performance, risk signals, and areas requiring intervention.

Act as a key point of contact for cross-regional operational issues and escalations, resolving immediate friction while converting recurring issues into structural improvements.

Design and implement scalable workflows, SOPs, SLAs, and intake mechanisms that improve consistency, reduce manual effort, and create a better experience for internal stakeholders and partners.

Introduce AI-enabled and automation-first workflows for intake, reporting, support, certification, and partner operations where they can safely improve speed, quality, and scale.

Collaborate closely with the Partner organization, Learning and Enablement, Professional Services, and other cross-functional teams to remove friction and improve execution across the partner ecosystem.

Partner closely with the broader operations business to drive cross-functional leverage of ideas and excellence, ensuring new methods and operational innovations are scaled beyond just partner operations.

Establish clear ownership models, decision rights, and governance guardrails to support regional nuance without creating shadow processes or operational inconsistencies.

Architect and maintain automated intake management workflows and SLA tracking mechanisms to optimize request processing and eliminate wait-time bottlenecks.

Establish standardized metric definitions and executive reporting frameworks that pair activity and outcome indicators to ensure reporting integrity across cross-functional teams.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience in Learning Operations, Program Management, Professional Services Operations, or a related operational leadership field in a high-growth technology environment.

Proven experience supporting global or multi-region teams and translating central strategy into executable operating plans.

Preferred experience in the Data & AI space, with a strong understanding of Databricks' platform capabilities, key differentiators, and end-to-end solutions, and the ability to work effectively with technical stakeholders.

Demonstrated ownership of operating cadence, forecasting, planning, and execution frameworks in a complex, matrixed environment.

Strong analytical capability and the ability to turn data into executive insight, operational decisions, and measurable business outcomes.

Experience improving processes and workflows, with a clear track record of reducing manual effort and increasing scale through automation or AI-enabled solutions.

Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions without direct authority.

Ability to work independently, manage priorities across time zones, and drive execution in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

Must be open to working a flexible schedule, including frequent late hours to accommodate discussions with the broader enablement team and partner liaisons, the majority of whom are based in the AMER timezone.

Demonstrated ability to drive cross-functional alignment and lead strategic delivery across matrixed global organizations.

Experience designing and optimizing workflow automation, structured intake management, and operational reporting engines with strict metric definition discipline.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in partner enablement, customer education, learning operations, or training operations.

Deep expertise working with and for System Integrators (SIs) and ISVs, with a strong grasp of their core operational principles and business models.

Fluency with AI tools, workflow automation, and analytics platforms used to streamline operations and generate actionable insights.

Strong commercial and operational acumen, including comfort with utilization, forecasting, partner spend, margin thinking, or RevOps-aligned execution.

Experience operating in a highly matrixed international environment with sensitivity to regional and cultural nuance.

Why Join Us

You will play a central role in shaping how partner enablement scales at Databricks.

This is a high-visibility role with meaningful impact, offering the opportunity to build a more efficient, governed, and AI-enabled operating model that helps our partner ecosystem grow with the business.

If you enjoy turning ambiguity into structure, building systems that remove friction, and helping teams scale through better operations rather than more manual work, this role is for you.

Operational Predictability: Build a disciplined partner enablement operating cadence where risks are surfaced early and execution is measurable and consistent.

Stakeholder Experience and Self-Sufficiency: Increase the percentage of standard partner enablement requests handled through structured, low-touch, or self-service workflows.

Escalation Management and Process Resilience: Reduce recurring operational friction by improving escalation handling, clarifying ownership, and improving systemic resolution of recurring issues.

Risk assessments. Policies, training, and governance. Develop and maintain internal privacy policies, external privacy notices, and standards. Design and deliver privacy training and awareness programs, and help operationalize privacy and AI governance frameworks and cross-functional privacy committees.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Legal Partnership: Build deep cross-functional relationships and collaborate with other legal leaders in commercial, go-to-market, compliance, corporate, and public affairs on privacy issues.

Business and Legal Judgment: Exercise practical judgment about when to approve, approve with conditions, decline, or escalate.

7+ years of relevant legal experience at a top law firm and/or in-house (a combination of both is a plus), with 5+ years focused on privacy and demonstrated experience building, operating, or leading a privacy compliance program (not solely advisory work)

Deep, current knowledge of global privacy and AI frameworks, including the GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, EU AI Act, and the growing patchwork of  U.S. state comprehensive privacy and AI laws, and familiarity with cross-border data transfer mechanisms (SCCs, IDTA, adequacy, EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework). 

Working knowledge of the operational building blocks of a privacy program — DPIAs/PIAs, ROPA and data mapping, data subject rights processes, privacy by design, and vendor/third-party risk management

Technical proficiency in using AI tools to build skills, agents, and other automated tasks.

Capacity to be a generalist and learn new areas of law and legal skills quickly as the business evolves

Deep understanding of cloud and software technology, and a strong desire to work on legal issues in these areas

Experience working for a company offering platform services to business customers is a plus

Familiarity with privacy management tooling (e.g., OneTrust or comparable) is a plus

J.D. from a top-tier law school

State bar membership required, in good standing

One or more privacy certifications (e.g., CIPP/E, CIPP/US, CIPM, CIPT, FIP) preferred; CIPM is particularly valued for a program-leadership role

You can set the direction for a program and drive it into execution — prioritizing and managing time and client expectations amid competing demands, often without direct guidance, as we scale our rapidly expanding business.

You exercise good judgment in raising issues, assessing risk, and providing concise, actionable, business-focused legal advice and counsel.

You build strong, deep working relationships with internal stakeholders across multiple geographies and functions, and are comfortable working with distributed teams.

P-1930

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data and AI teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers — and customer-obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to solve technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started.

As part of the AI team, you'll build the platforms and products that power everything from data apps, AI agents, model training, model serving, and Vector Search. You'll be joining a high-agency, high-visibility team operating at the frontier of AI infrastructure — with deep ties to research, product, and real-world enterprise use cases. Databricks Mosaic AI is one of our fastest-growing businesses, helping thousands of our customers democratize AI within their organizations. We're building the products and infrastructure that power the next generation of AI.

The Foundation Model Inference team is the backbone of Databricks’ generative AI capabilities. We build the infrastructure that enables our customers to serve, scale, and optimize frontier models with enterprise-grade reliability and performance. Our Foundation Model APIs provide a unified platform that gives customers access to LLMs with the governance, flexibility, and scalability required for enterprise production workloads.

We are looking for high-agency engineers who are excited to work on powering model inference at enterprise scale.

Build LLM infrastructure powering large-scale inference workloads for customers through partner models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini) and self-hosted models (Qwen, GPT-OSS, Llama)

Collaborate with platform, infra, and ML teams to deliver seamless end-to-end experiences

Shape how developers and data scientists build and interact with AI on Databricks

8+ years of experience in backend or infrastructure engineering

Experience with real-time serving, ML infrastructure, or GPU orchestration

Familiarity with service-oriented architecture, deployment pipelines, and system observability

Exposure to platforms like SageMaker, Vertex AI, or Azure ML

Databricks is seeking a Director, Marketing Strategy and AI Transformation to own how our global marketing organization decides where to invest and reimagine how the work gets done. You will set the planning and investment operating model for marketing while leading the shift from human-executed to agent-executed work across the organization. This highly cross-functional role partners closely with Marketing Leadership and their departments, Finance, Sales Strategy and our central platform and data teams to make investment decisions that are grounded in real capacity and to turn AI capability into standard practice at scale.

Own the end-to-end annual marketing planning process, establishing a single planning system of record with explicit trade-offs 

Evaluate leading indicators and business outcomes to understand low and high performance areas and drivers

Identify and scale best practices to drive incremental growth across global business units

Build and maintain the marketing capacity model spanning people, agencies, and agent-based execution, so that commitments are made against known capacity constraints

Oversee development of the highest-leverage marketing workflows for agent execution, targeting a step-change improvement in time-to-market

Align marketing investment strategy against the company's strategic bets, ensuring clarity on spend and capacity toward the highest-impact products and programs, and improving pipeline efficiency.

Drive marketing target setting in partnership with Marketing, Finance and Sales Strategy, establishing a transparent methodology which can shift agilely with the business

Drive agent adoption across the global marketing organization and establish org-wide standards for prompts, context, and agent workflows, measured by sustained change in time to market. 

Establish AI governance and adoption guardrails for agent-based marketing, setting standards for quality, risk, data privacy, and responsible use, so that adoption scales safely and consistently. 

Build and develop a high-performing team from the ground up, and model and reinforce Databricks' culture principles.

Deep experience in marketing strategy, marketing planning, marketing operations, or GTM/revenue operations in a B2B environment within SaaS or enterprise technology, including ownership of an annual planning or investment allocation cycle at scale.

Demonstrated experience redesigning workflows around AI, including hands-on work building agent workflows, writing and iterating prompts, and structuring context

Track record of driving sustained behavior change across a large, matrixed organization, with evidence that adoption persisted beyond the initial rollout.

Expertise in how a marketing organization operates end to end across demand generation, campaign operations, content production, field and events, brand, and analytics

job_title: Specialist Solutions Architect - Azure Infrastructure & AI Platform
job_description:
FEQ427R143

As an Infrastructure & AI Platform Specialist Solutions Architect (SSA), you will serve as a trusted technical advisor, guiding enterprise customers through the architecture, cloud infrastructure, and AI deployment patterns of their Databricks Platform on Microsoft Azure. You combine deep technical expertise with strategic thinking to position Databricks as the foundation of your customers’ data and AI strategy.

This role can be remote.

The impact you will have

Guide strategic customers through the full lifecycle of Databricks on Azure, including platform administration, from initial architectural design to production deployment

Architect and scale compute/networking infrastructure designed specifically for AI workloads, enterprise LLM deployments, and high-performance GenAI applications built on Databricks

Serve as a subject matter expert in core areas such as Microsoft Azure infrastructure, infrastructure-as-code (IaC), cloud networking, and identity management

Drive technical wins in competitive scenarios by demonstrating Databricks’ differentiation through custom-built solutions

Orchestrate cross-functional resources (DSAs, SAs, SSAs, Partners) to deliver comprehensive solutions for complex customer needs

Influence product direction by providing structured feedback on customer requirements and competitive gaps

What We Look For

6+ years in solutions architecture, technical pre-sales, or a senior hands-on technical role

Hands-on experience architecting underlying cloud infrastructure for AI/ML execution—including accelerator configuration (GPUs/TPUs), scalable model serving infrastructure, vectorized data retrieval, and balancing cloud performance vs. cost for large-scale AI workloads

Advanced expertise across the following areas:

Security & Identity: Azure security controls, platform/network/data security, encryption, vulnerability management, compliance, and identity protocols (Microsoft Entra ID / SCIM, OAuth, SAML, Federation)

Networking & Deployments: Azure enterprise networking (VNet peering, ExpressRoute, Private Link), network routing, performance optimization, and large-scale deployment management

Platform Administration: High availability, disaster recovery, cluster orchestration, observability (Azure Monitor, Log Analytics), and Azure cost management

Infrastructure Automation (InfraOps): Hands-on automation using IaC tools (e.g., Terraform, Bicep, ARM) to build, maintain, and scale complex Azure environments

Contract & Order Oversight: Support local contract execution workflows on behalf of the entity, ensuring all EU customer order forms and cloud services agreements adhere to established commercial and legal guardrails.

Intercompany & Revenue Operations Support: Oversee local revenue processes, including EU customer contracting, billing workflows, and payment collection oversight, coordinating closely with Global Order-to-Cash (OtC) and Treasury teams to ensure proper fund-remittance to Databricks, Inc. and compliance with intercompany remittance timelines.

Global Revenue Assurance Strategy & Execution

Team Leadership: Lead, mentor, and scale a global team of revenue accounting professionals, fostering a collaborative, high-performance culture.

ASC 606 / IFRS 15 & Technical Accounting Compliance: Ensure consistent treatment and proper accounting of global enterprise SaaS and consumption-based revenue transactions in compliance with ASC 606, U.S. GAAP, and internal accounting policies. Experience applying differences in IFRS 15 vs. ASC 606 in local statutory accounting. 

Deal Strategy & Commercial Advisory: Partner with Global Sales, Strategic Pricing, Deal Desk, and Legal functions during deal negotiations to structure non-standard, complex customer contracts in compliance with revenue recognition standards.

Delegated Approval Authority: Exercise tiered finance approval authority for non-standard pricing and commercial terms within established guardrails.

Cross-Functional Process Innovation: Collaborate with FP&A, IT, RevOps, and Order-to-Cash teams to identify data, process, and automation improvements (e.g., system enhancements, SQL data analysis) to minimize manual workarounds and scale operations.

Training & Enablement: Develop and deliver technical revenue recognition training to cross-functional business partners.

What we look for:

Professional License: Active Chartered Accountant (ACA / FCA / ACCA) qualification required.

Big 4 Experience: Minimum 5+ years of audit or advisory experience at a Big 4 accounting firm (Deloitte, PwC, EY, or KPMG).

戦略的アカウントにおける複雑なユースケースおよび複数のワークストリーム全体で、技術的な実行戦略を定義し、影響を与える。

お客様の成果を加速させる実用的なソリューション、プロトタイプ、再利用可能な技術資産を構築・実証する。

Databricks、お客様、導入チームと連携し、リソースの調整、リスク管理、デリバリーの加速を行う。

分散データシステム、データエンジニアリング、分析、データウェアハウジング、AI/ML、および最新のクラウドアーキテクチャに関する深い理解

安全でガバナンスが効き、スケーラブルかつ本番環境に対応したデータソリューションを設計した経験

不明確な技術的問題を解決し、トレードオフを評価し、構造化された分析や実験を通じてソリューションを検証する能力

Multi-cloud is core to Databricks product strategy. Compute serves as the layer that abstracts the cloud from the rest of the company. Building unified infrastructure on top of heterogeneous clouds is a challenge that few companies experience.

Work alongside industry experts who have built world-class systems like Borg, Kubernetes, and Uber’s infrastructure.

job_description:
Deeply understanding what’s in the enterprise data has been a challenge that Databricks has been addressing by providing analytics and machine learning tools. From data warehousing with Databricks SQL to large-scale distributed processing with Spark and advanced ML tools for experimentation and model serving, we empower our customers to gain insights and drive innovation.

To enable all of this on Databricks, making data ingestion seamless is crucial. That’s the mission of the Ingestion Core Team: to make the ingestion of all data—structured and unstructured—simple, reliable, and efficient. Simplifying the complex is hard, and that’s where you come in. This role requires building distributed platform systems to incrementally ingest high-volume, petabyte-scale data from diverse sources—including cloud storage (SQS, ADLS, GCS), databases (Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, Postgres), and file sources (Google Drive, SharePoint)—at high throughput and low cost. The data includes structured formats (JSON, Parquet, CSV) as well as unstructured data (text, images, docs, PPTs, and blobs), all of which land in Delta Lake with schema evolution and change data capture (CDC) capabilities.

Join us in making data ingestion effortless and be part of the team that powers the future of AI + data at Databricks!

As an engineer on the team, you will work on projects that:

Build distributed infrastructure to ingest data from diverse sources and support streaming ingestion, incremental processing, and replication. This isn’t just about building plugin connectors.

Reduce end-to-end latency, increase throughput, and reduce costs from the time data appears in source systems to when it is available in Delta Lake.

Design and optimize streaming and distributed workloads for throughput, cost, latency, reliability, and scale.

Optimize streaming workloads by exploring and applying ML techniques.

Build monitoring and observability capabilities (customer-facing and internal) that provide visibility into ingestion workflows and the systems running them.

Collaborate with partner teams to enable use cases like RAG and AI agents.

Build Agentic SDKs with strong evaluations.

Ideal Engineer should have:

5+ years of experience writing production code in one of: Java, Scala, Go, C++, or Python.

Experience architecting, developing, and deploying large-scale distributed and asynchronous systems.

Experience with distributed systems, streaming, Spark, databases, data processing, or CDC.

Experience building or operating systems where scale, throughput, latency, reliability, and cost are important considerations.

Comfortable using AI tools and defining effective evals to shorten the development loop.

FEQ227R209

About the Role

Databricks needs to understand what technical capability looks like across several large, fast-moving populations: employees, customers, and partners. Today that happens through role-based learning pathways and product-aligned enablement, an approach that can't keep pace with how quickly the platform, technology, and roles change. AI has also collapsed the half-life of technical proficiency, and for the first time, it makes a living, self-maintaining model of capability possible.

In this builder role, you'll own systems for defining, measuring, and developing technical capability across Databricks learner audiences. You'll build a capability model that ties roles, skills, content, and credentials together and the instrumentation that shows where capability actually stands.

What You'll Own

Skills taxonomies, capability models, and learning context

Define the skills taxonomies that make up technical capability and shape how they’re organized; what skills exist, which are adjacent, which are prerequisites, how quickly they go stale, and what sources are available to learners for developing and maintaining them.

Observability and measurement

Stand up instrumentation and AI-informed signals that show where capability stands and where it's drifting. Develop live signals, not a quarterly or monthly health index, to show how skills are moving and evolving.

Anticipate where capability demand is heading. Product releases, market shifts, and role evolution are constant; track changes closely so emerging skills surface early and content and programs stay ahead of change.

AI-native tooling

Build the software that maintains the skills taxonomy and capability model, including LLM-driven skill extraction and organization, agentic pipelines that keep them current, automated drift and gap detection, and APIs that expose it all.

Make the model reusable enterprise context that other systems, teams, and products build on vs. a training-only asset.

Impact You'll Have

You will sit upstream of and across several teams and functions:

Anywhere skills show up in products: You define what technical capability means and what evidence counts, so wherever skills are inferred, captured, or recognized, it reflects real technical work and skills & abilities.

Content and curriculum. The skills taxonomy and capability model influence what gets built next and why. Learning context is a critical input to generative content.

Learning architecture and in-product training: Your work informs what learning belongs where and how it’s presented. Pathways are assembled with the model and taxonomy instead of mapped by hand; in-product training surfaces them to learners.

Certification & accreditation. The capability model grounds skills assessment to guide and accelerate exam developers.

Learning & enablement. You give the organization a current view of capability across every audience, and a shared model to build and plan against.

What We're Looking For

Experience in technical training, learning, enablement, or product education in data & AI, cloud, or comparable product categories.

Experience designing capability or skills models and the systems around them, spanning modeling, measurement, and instrumentation.

A builder mindset. Ability to use Python and SQL and build apps, with AI assistance, and wire up pipelines and stand up tooling yourself.

AI-native. AI tooling is how you build and reason, from extraction and assessment to agentic workflows and evaluation. You understand when to reach for AI and when not.

A track record of moving strategy as an IC through analysis and clear writing.

Nice to Have

Familiarity with off-the-shelf skills-intelligence tooling and build-vs-buy tradeoffs.

Experience instrumenting capability data across several audiences.

What Success Looks Like in Year One

A live skills taxonomy, capability model, and learning context resources are published, and content, learning, and certification teams plan against them.

Decisions about what to build, refresh, or retire leverage the skills taxonomy and capability model, so content better keeps pace with the product, and investment goes where capability demand and skill gaps are real.

In-product training uses the model to target and measure learning, so learners can see what moves them forward, and stakeholders get insight into skills attainment within their audiences.

Teams that bring skills into products work from the same model, so a skill means the same thing wherever someone encounters it.

Ground decisions in evidence - use research instincts and real usage to pressure-test ideas and know what to build next.

Staff-level scope and impact. A track record of shipping complex, high-quality developer products and leading design direction on hard problems.

Enterprise customers are investing in AI, but most are stuck between a successful pilot and real organizational adoption. The gap is not technology. It is whether the workforce can change how it works.

You will own end-to-end workforce transformation engagements with Databricks' largest customers. You will diagnose where a customer's workforce is today, define what needs to change, build the transformation plan, and drive execution until adoption sticks. You are the directly responsible individual for each engagement, not a contributor to someone else's project.

The Impact You Will Have

Own the full transformation lifecycle for each customer, from workforce assessment through capability pathways, operating rhythm, and measurement. You build the plan and you execute it.

Run 2 to 3 concurrent engagements across different formats. These range from short-cycle assessments (2 to 4 weeks) to coached transformations (8 to 12 weeks) to deep embedded engagements (12 to 16 weeks). You will manage a mixed portfolio simultaneously.

Design for multiple organizational layers within a single engagement. That means building executive sponsorship with CDOs, CIOs, and CHROs while also architecting the manager enablement and individual contributor adoption layers underneath.

Drive execution, not just planning. You will stand up the operating rhythm, coach internal champions, unblock adoption barriers, and adjust the plan when reality diverges from the model.

Design the human-agent collaboration model for each customer's workforce. Assess workflows and distinguish what should stay human from what should be automated, agent-assisted, or fully agent-led. Design differentiated pathways for builders in technical roles and users in workflow roles.

Shape how engagements are scoped and priced. You are closest to the work and will ensure that commercial commitments are deliverable.

Turn what you learn into repeatable tools and playbooks that can scale beyond practitioner-led delivery.

Partner with technical deployment, AI transformation, and account teams. Other teams build and land the solution. You own what happens after.

job_description:
RDQ427R630

This role is in-person and Bay-Area-based by design, so you can be in the room with founders and investors.

At Databricks, we are obsessed with enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from security threat detection to cancer drug development. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform, so our customers can focus on the high-value challenges central to their missions. Founded in 2013 by the original creators of Apache Spark™, Databricks has grown from a tiny corner office in Berkeley, CA, to a global organization with over 11,000 employees. Thousands of organizations, from small startups to Fortune 100, trust Databricks with their mission-critical workloads, making us one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in the world and one of the top 5 most valuable private companies.

About the Role:

Databricks works with founders from the earliest days of their companies, when it is still just a team, an idea, and a lot of unproven AI. The Technical Business Development Manager for the Startup and VC Ecosystem owns the operational engine and the relationships behind that work, and the role is technical. You will run our startup program day to day, sit across from early-stage founders and talk seriously about their AI systems, produce a steady cadence of founder and investor events in San Francisco, and work hand in hand with the events teams at the venture firms whose founders we most want to reach. You will work closely with Databricks Ventures. This role is built to grow: you will start close to the program, the founders, and the events, and over time, take on more of the relationships and the strategy for how Databricks engages the startup ecosystem end-to-end.

This role asks for four things that rarely sit in one person: the discipline of an operator who tracks every applicant and commitment without dropping one, the hands of a builder who is genuinely fluent in AI and can talk to a founder as a peer, the ease of someone who earns the trust of founders and the partners at the best venture firms in the country, and the judgment to turn all of that into strategy for how Databricks wins the next generation of companies. Most strong candidates have two of these, and some have three. We are hiring for trajectory: you should already be strong in the operating and the building, and hungry to grow into relationships and strategy. This is one of the rare seats where operating, building, and relationship-building are the same job. 

The impact you will have: 

Run the startup program: Own the day-to-day operations of the program, including applicant intake, evaluation, scoring, routing, and offer decisions, with precise tracking of every applicant, commitment, and outcome. Run it on AI automation built with Databricks AI tooling such as Omnigent, Unity Gateway, Agent Bricks, etc. Strong, hands-on proficiency with these tools is a requirement, not just knowing your way around them.

Bring programmatic discipline: Own the trackers, the automation, the quality bar, and the follow-through so that nothing falls through the cracks.

Be technical with founders: Hold real technical conversations with early-stage founders about their models, agents, data, and automation, and where Databricks and Neon fit. Earn their trust by being credible on the technology, not by pitching.

Build and prototype: Build the automation and internal tooling that runs the program, and stay hands-on with the same AI tools founders use, so you can assess their technical ideas from a place of experience. This is developer relations at its most technical: close to the code and close to the builders.

Assess and translate: Assess each founder's technical capability and the strength of their idea, and carry what you learn back to Product and to Databricks Ventures.

Run founder and investor events: Design and run a regular calendar of founder and investor gatherings in San Francisco, including dinners, workshops, office hours, and demo-day tie-ins. Partner with the events and platform teams at leading venture firms to co-produce these gatherings, and build durable relationships with those teams that deepen over time.

Represent Databricks in the ecosystem: Show up as a founder-first, technically credible presence at founder and investor events, and grow into being one of the faces of Databricks across the venture community.

Grow into ownership: Work alongside Databricks Ventures on how we engage founders across the full arc of their journey, from a first look at their technology and ideas to whatever they build next, and grow into broader ownership of the startup function as you build trust and results.

What we look for: 

This is a rare combination, and we know it. We are hiring for trajectory as much as for a finished resume: the strongest candidates are already strong on the first three and eager to grow into the rest.

Genuinely technical with AI. You build. You can prototype an automation, reason about an agent architecture, and get into the details of a founder's stack without hand-waving.

A programmatic operator with an obsessive eye for detail. You run complex, multi-track programs without dropping a thread.

The developer-relations instinct. You earn credibility with builders by being one, and you can explain and teach hard technical ideas clearly.

We are looking for a Lead Solution Architect focused on Generative AI to support our EMEA Emerging Digital Natives and Startups business unit — one of the fastest-moving, most technically ambitious patches in EMEA. You will be the go-to expert our Account Teams and customers turn to when a GenAI or LLM use case needs to move from an ambitious idea to a production-grade reality across our high-growth accounts.

This is a highly technical, customer-facing individual contributor role for someone who lives at the frontier of applied GenAI. You will shape architectures, prove out the hard problems, challenge and influence customer roadmaps, and raise the GenAI capability of the entire EMEA Emerging DNB field organisation.

Serve as the deep technical authority on Generative AI, LLMs, and applied machine learning for the EMEA Emerging DNB business unit, supporting the most strategic and complex customer engagements across our digital-native and born-in-the-cloud accounts.

Partner with our EMEA Emerging DNB Solutions Architects, Solutions Engineers, and Account teams to scope, design, and de-risk GenAI use cases — from retrieval-augmented generation and agentic systems to fine-tuning and evaluation.

Build hands-on proofs of concept and reference implementations that operationalise large-scale LLM and deep learning workloads on Databricks (Mosaic AI, MLflow, Model Serving, Vector Search, Unity Catalog governance), tuned to the fast iteration cycles Emerging DNB customers expect.

Lead fine-tuning and model-customisation engagements on open LLMs (e.g., Llama-family models), including judge-based and label-efficient evaluation approaches for domains where quality and safety are paramount.

Act as a bridge to Product and Engineering — channel field and customer feedback into the roadmap and represent the roadmap back to the field.

Enable and mentor the broader EMEA Emerging DNB Field Engineering team through workshops, reference architectures, and internal enablement, multiplying GenAI expertise across our ~70-person SA/SE organisation.

Strong understanding of the LLM landscape, including leading proprietary and open-source models and providers, with the ability to differentiate their capabilities, trade-offs, and suitability for different use cases, and to articulate a clear, informed point of view (POV) to customers.

Deep expertise in the modern GenAI stack: LLM application patterns (RAG, agents, tool use), fine-tuning and model customization, prompt and evaluation engineering, and LLM guardrails/safety.

Strong foundations in machine learning and deep learning, including distributed training, GPU workloads, and the full MLOps lifecycle (tracking, registry, serving, monitoring).

Proficiency in Python and the ML ecosystem (PyTorch/Transformers, MLflow, Spark), and comfort building production-quality reference implementations.

Experience with the Databricks platform — or the ability to ramp on it quickly — including Mosaic AI, Model Serving, Vector Search, and Unity Catalog. Cloud experience across AWS, Azure, or GCP.

Excellent communication and consultative skills: able to earn the trust of both hands-on engineers and senior technical executives, and to explain complex GenAI trade-offs clearly.

A track record of technical leadership and mentorship — someone who elevates the people around them.

Comfort operating at the pace of digital-native and high-growth customers, where speed, iteration, and technical credibility win the deal.

Based in the United Kingdom and able to work across EMEA time zones, with willingness to travel to customer sites within the region as needed.

Background helping digital-native customers build data and ML solutions (e.g., prior experience at a data/ML platform or consulting vendor) is a strong plus.

Nice to Have

Public technical presence: conference speaking, published talks, blogs, or open-source contributions in the ML/GenAI space.

Domain depth in a regulated or high-stakes industry (healthcare/life sciences, financial services) where model quality, evaluation, and safety are critical.

Experience partnering with Product and Engineering teams to influence roadmap.

You will work on the hardest and most exciting GenAI problems our EMEA Emerging DNB customers have — companies building the future in real time — with the platform and the people to actually solve them, not just advise. job_description:
P-1096

At Databricks, we run the world's largest AI platform. We believe the next breakthroughs will come from models trained on domain-specific enterprise data, not from bigger general-purpose models alone.

That's why we built AI Runtime, a serverless product that makes GPU training of any size feel simple, so companies can train their own models the way frontier labs do. Customers across industries train on it, right next to the enterprise data already in Databricks. Among them are Rivian in automotive, Robinhood in fintech, and Merck, which builds foundation models for drug discovery. Our own AI researchers use it to post-train models with hundreds of billions to nearly a trillion parameters.

It takes a lot of engineering to make that work, and we've written about it on our blog: how we keep GPUs reliable, make training fault-tolerant, and speed up fine-tuning with fused kernels and smart sequence packing. AI agents now launch experiments too, and on our research team they've already increased training jobs 8x.

As a Senior Staff Software Engineer, you'll work on the systems behind all of this, solving the hardest technical problems and shaping where AI Runtime goes next.

The impact you will have:

Drive AI Runtime's architecture and lead Databricks' long-term technical direction in AI training infrastructure.

Define the reliability and observability strategy for a fleet that keeps growing in scale and complexity.

Shape AI Runtime's developer experience for people and agents, so even the largest training jobs feel as simple as a first experiment.

Anticipate industry trends and choose the technical bets that prepare AI Runtime for new GPU generations and workload types.

As a Sr. Sales Compensation Analyst on the Comp Admin team, you will run commissions administration from start to finish for a large global group of sellers, so they can trust that they are paid accurately and on time. You will own a large payee portfolio with no supervision needed, from plan rollout through calculation, payroll, and follow-up support. You will catch issues before they reach the field and keep every step audit-ready. You will also use AI and automation every day to make our work faster, more accurate, and easier to scale as Databricks grows.

The impact you will have:

Own commissions administration for a large payee portfolio with no errors: user setup, plan distribution, input processing, calculation, and payment.

Deliver plan rollout and payout accurately and on time every cycle, including tracking ICPW acceptance and preparing data that feeds payroll and accounting deadlines.

Resolve payee and partner questions quickly and fully, so issues are settled the first time without escalations. Run rep training and enablement sessions as needed.

Keep your portfolio fully compliant with SOX and audit requirements by following controls with discipline, documenting clearly, and keeping evidence reproducible.

Find discrepancies, exceptions, and control gaps early (for example, wrong credits, quota mismatches, or cap and accelerator errors), trace the root cause in the data, and drive the fix with Sales Ops, Payroll, and Accounting.

Make recurring workflows faster, more reliable, and easier to repeat by improving documentation, simplifying handoffs, and cutting rework.

Use AI to improve recurring work such as validations, reconciliations, and responses to comp questions. Build repeatable approaches that others on the team can adopt.

Help the team grow by mentoring new hires on tools, processes, and best practices, and by referring strong candidates.

What we look for:

5+ years of hands-on sales compensation administration, including user setup, plan distribution, calculation and payment, comp questions, and rep training.

Advanced Xactly skills, including administration, reporting, and troubleshooting, with the ability to resolve system issues on your own.

Advanced Excel and Google Workspace skills for complex modeling, data analysis, and reconciliation.

A solid grasp of SaaS go-to-market compensation models (commit vs. consumption, quotas, OTI, accelerators, overlays, SPIFFs, MBOs) and how plan mechanics shape seller behavior.

Experience working under SOX or similar audit controls, with accurate, well-documented work and clean audit trails.

Strong analytical judgment: you investigate patterns, find root causes, and turn data into practical recommendations.

Comfort using AI tools and LLMs in daily work, plus the judgment to check outputs for accuracy before relying on them.

Clear communication and teamwork across time zones with global partners in Sales Ops, Payroll, Accounting, and Sales leadership.

GAQ128R86

Mission

Databricks is looking for a Senior Manager, Payroll to own end-to-end payroll delivery for the Europe region. This is a hands-on leadership role — you will run the operations, lead the team, own the compliance, and be the subject matter expert the business turns to when it matters.

You will sit within the Global Payroll function, reporting directly to the Director, Global Payroll Operations, contributing to global strategy, cross-regional alignment, and function-wide initiatives beyond your direct remit.

You will manage a team of two to five payroll professionals and be accountable for accurate, timely, and compliant payroll for a fast-scaling workforce.

This is not a coordinator role with a manager title. We need someone who has been in the engine room, knows what good looks like, and can build it here.

Individual will not be ‘back office’ this is a business facing role and enhancing employee experience and stakeholder management is key. 

The impact you will have:

Payroll Operations

Own the full payroll cycle, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and a clean audit trail on every run

Manage the payroll calendar, cut-off deadlines, and coordination with HR and Finance to ensure data integrity from hire to final pay

Serve as the primary escalation point for payroll discrepancies, employee queries, and operational issues — resolving with speed and precision

Drive continuous improvement across payroll processes, reducing manual effort and increasing controls without sacrificing responsiveness

Drive high performance from payroll vendors.

Technology & Systems

Work with our Payroll GPO and Leadership team to build Data and AI enabled payroll operations

Identify opportunities to reduce manual reconciliation and improve data accuracy across the payroll tech stack

Tax Compliance  

Good understanding of requirements outside the payslip (such as PSA and STBV in UK) and able to input and work with relevant teams to ensure compliance. 

Equity & Supplemental Compensation

Manage payroll processing and tax withholding for RSU vesting events, including coordination with Stock Administration on vest schedules, sell-to-cover mechanics, and supplemental withholding rates

Partner with Legal and Tax on equity income sourcing and reporting obligations on equity-derived income

Reconcile equity payroll data to stock admin records each quarter with zero tolerance for mismatch

Team Leadership

Lead, develop, and performance-manage a team of payroll professionals — setting clear expectations, managing workload, and building capability

Expected to take a broader leadership role across the Global Payroll team as a senior leader within it. 

Create a team culture where accuracy is non-negotiable, deadlines are owned not managed around, and problems surface early

Build redundancy and cross-training so the function is never single-threaded 

Coach the team on technical depth — tax law, equity mechanics, compliance — so they grow into the next generation of payroll leaders

Controls, Audit & Governance

Design and maintain SOX-compliant payroll controls, including segregation of duties, approval workflows, and exception reporting

Lead payroll's response to internal and external audits — preparing documentation, managing timelines, and closing findings without repeat

Maintain payroll policy documentation and desktop procedures, updated with every legislative or system change

Produce monthly payroll metrics and variance analysis for Finance and HR leadership

What we look for:

8+ years of hands-on payroll experience, with at least 5 years in a leadership role managing a team

Deep working knowledge of European Payrolls 

Proven experience managing RSU and equity payroll — from vest event processing through reconciliation

Strong command of payroll reconciliation, general ledger mapping, and accrual processes

Experience leading teams of four or more people — you know how to delegate, develop, and hold people accountable

Excellent business stakeholder management skills - comms and employee experience focus

GAQ128R85

Databricks is looking for a Senior Collections Analyst to own a high-volume accounts receivable (AR) portfolio in a fast-growing, usage-based SaaS business. The role drives timely collections, reduces delinquency, protects cash flow and leads recovery on complex, high-value accounts, while helping shape credit risk decisions. Working closely with Sales, Legal, Billing, Revenue Operations, Cash Application and Finance leadership to resolve disputes, billing gaps and customer escalations, the role has a measurable impact on DSO and bad debt exposure and requires regular overlap with EMEA and PST business hours.

Job Description

Own end-to-end portfolio collections and recovery strategies, partnering cross-functionally to resolve high-value escalations, influence credit risk decisions, and drive measurable performance across DSO, aging buckets, and bad debt exposure.

Design and run recovery strategies for accounts that are structurally delinquent or high-risk.

Lead cross-functional escalation forums for disputed high-value accounts.

Present portfolio-level risk trends and actionable insights to Finance leadership.

Recommend credit limit changes, payment term changes or account holds based on behavioral analytics.

Work with Legal on pre-legal actions and structured recovery plans.

Assess creditworthiness, establish risk controls, and lead complex recoveries to protect working capital and minimize bad debt exposure.

Build scalable reporting models that give clear visibility into aging, dispute velocity and payment predictability.

Flag worsening payment patterns, and provide quarterly bad debt reserve inputs with documented risk rationale for each account.

Act as the subject matter expert on usage-based billing disputes and contract interpretation. Resolve complex disputes about usage, contract terms and invoicing discrepancies.

Handle exceptions from automated dunning, and lead the clean-up of aged AR.

Manage high-volume customer communication and escalations in Collections Tool, with structured follow-through.

Work with Cash Application to keep unapplied cash low and resolve posting gaps.

Find the systemic billing, consumption or process gaps that cause repeat delinquency. Work with Billing and Revenue Operations to put corrective frameworks in place.

Perform detailed account reconciliations in NetSuite to keep AR accurate and audit-ready.

Help standardize collections processes so they are faster and can scale, and support user acceptance testing (UAT) for new or improved systems.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Finance or Accounting is a must. Additional Accounting Qualification is a plus.

10+ years of collections experience, ideally with both public/private technology companies.

A track record of owning large, complex, high-value AR portfolios with measurable impact on DSO and cash.

Working knowledge of usage-based billing models and contract structures.

Demonstrated ownership of high-value, complex AR portfolios with material cash impact.

A proven ability to influence commercial stakeholders in high-pressure recovery situations.

Experience supporting reserve discussions and credit risk decisions.

Strong commercial judgment, balancing revenue protection against the risk to customer relationships.

Ability to synthesize large data sets into executive-level risk insights.

Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.

Hands-on experience with NetSuite / Salesforce with fluency with AI tools, including automated dunning solutions is preferred.

CSQ128R189

As a Forward Deployment Strategist (FDS), you are the critical bridge between a customer's multi-million dollar business problem and Databricks' technical solution. You are a product manager for the field, owning the entire non-technical lifecycle of an FDE engagement.

You will partner with our Account Executives to build C-suite trust, perform deep discovery to map the customer's political and technical landscape, and, most importantly, scope the value. You will define the Minimum Viable Product for a pilot, write the PRD that guides the engineering team, and manage the project to a successful landing.

This role requires a rare mix of C-suite gravitas, deep product-style thinking, and a hands-on, get it done execution mindset.

You will report to the Director, Forward Deployed Engineering.

The impact you will have:

C-Suite Scoping & Value Definition: Partner with Sales to perform deep discovery, map the customer's organization, quantify the business value ($10M+ problems), and define the pilot (MVP, success criteria, timeline).

End-to-End Product Ownership: Act as the CEO of the project by authoring the PRD, prioritizing the engineering backlog, relentlessly managing scope, and acting as the primary hands-on QA tester.

Agile Project Execution & Delivery: Drive the FDE build team via an agile process, manage all stakeholder communications from the C-suite to individual engineers, and act as the escalation manager to unblock all technical or political issues.

Solution Launch & Landing: Own the Day 0 launch, manage the war room, and drive the solution from launch to full adoption by capturing user feedback, iterating, and proving the defined business value.

Strategic Handoff & Growth: Scope the ongoing maintenance plan, create customer documentation/training, and leverage your trusted advisor status to identify the next high-value FDE engagement.

What we look for:

Executive Presence & Communication: A Trusted Advisor with C-suite gravitas and superb communication skills. You are opinionated, humble, and can build rapport and drive decisions in days, not weeks.

Product & Strategy Mindset: A Product Thinker and Systems Thinker who can perform a SWOT analysis, understand a competitive landscape, and define what to build and why.

Relentless Execution: An Execution Driver with a Hands-On mentality. You are relentless, an expert at escalation, and willing to do the unglamorous work to get the project done.

Ideal Experience: 2+ years as a Deployment Strategist OR 2+ years at a high-growth startup in a builder or founder capacity. (Alternatively: 5+ years in a senior, client-facing product or delivery role at a top-tier tech company or consultancy).

Proven Skills: Demonstrated experience in value-based scoping (TCO/ROI), managing agile software projects, writing PRDs, and the ability/interest to travel up to 50%.

CSQ128R185

The Engagement Manager (EM) within Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) translates customer business challenges into outcome-driven FDE engagements, leading the entire lifecycle from early opportunity discovery and deal shaping to contract closure and seamless handover to the delivery team.

In this role, you will define measurable success criteria aligned with the customer’s strategic priorities and bridge them into actionable service scopes and commercial contracts. Serving as a business and commercial lead connecting customer strategy, services sales, and delivery operations, you will drive FDE bookings, services revenue, and platform adoption across Databricks.

You will collaborate closely with Account Executives, Field Engineering, customer executives, FDE technical leadership, and strategic partners to drive consensus and execution across opportunity qualification, SOW creation, pricing, funding strategy, pipeline forecasting, and delivery enablement.

You will report to the Director, Forward Deployed Engineering.

The Impact You Will Have 

Lead Value-Driven Opportunity Shaping & Platform Positioning: Engage early with account teams and customers to uncover business priorities, budget, and executive sponsorship, while articulating customer success stories and tangible business ROI to qualify high-impact FDE engagements (or route to partners) and drive Databricks platform adoption and expansion. 

Drive Commercial Structuring & Co-Funding Models: Formulate innovative commercial deal structures and unlock co-investment/funding vehicles across Databricks, CSPs (AWS, Azure, GCP), and strategic partners to solve customer budget constraints. 

Own the End-to-End Services Sales Cycle: Lead the full deal execution lifecycle—including solution scoping, proposal and Statement of Work (SOW) drafting, level-of-effort estimation, pricing models, internal approval governance, and commercial contract negotiations. 

Manage Pipeline Governance & Forecasting Accuracy: Maintain disciplined oversight of deal pipeline health, major milestones, risks, and forecasts to deliver predictable bookings and services revenue projections to sales and delivery leadership. 

Collaborative Delivery Architecture, Handoff & Partner Alignment: Cultivate trusted executive relationships and align with SI/consulting partners, collaborating closely with FDE technical leadership to define clear scopes, dependencies, and staffing plans that ensure a seamless transition from contract signature to execution. 

What We Look For 

Senior Customer-Facing & Commercial Track Record: 7+ years of proven experience in enterprise professional services, management consulting, or technical services sales, demonstrating strong executive presence, negotiation skills, and a track record of shaping and closing complex commercial deals. 

Value Framing & Comprehensive Deal Crafting: Proven ability to translate complex business objectives into clear value propositions, measurable success metrics, and actionable SOWs, backed by hands-on experience in drafting proposals, building pricing models, navigating internal approvals, and commercial negotiations. 

Data & AI Domain Literacy & Executive Advisory: Solid understanding of the Data & AI landscape (cloud architecture, data engineering, analytics, ML/AI) with the ability to articulate technical services in terms of business value/ROI and lead credible strategic discussions with both technical and C-level stakeholders. 

Pipeline Governance & Delivery Alignment: Demonstrated accountability for deal pipeline management, bookings/revenue forecasting, and risk mitigation, combined with a working knowledge of project delivery governance to ensure smooth post-sale handover and stakeholder alignment. 

Language Proficiency: Native-level fluency in Korean and professional working proficiency in English (both written and verbal). 

Preferred Qualifications 

Advanced Data & AI Deal & Contract Structuring: Experience leading business development, scoping, and contracting for Data & AI platform modernization, enterprise migrations, or generative AI solutions, including experience structuring outcome-based, milestone-driven, or fixed-scope contracts. 

Cloud Ecosystem & Partner Co-Delivery Models: In-depth familiarity with major cloud providers (AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud) and leveraging CSP co-funding/incentive programs, alongside experience designing joint engagement or subcontracting models with System Integrators (SIs) and delivery partners. 

Korea Enterprise Market & Procurement Expertise: Proven track record of leading large-scale enterprise engagements across key Korean industries (Financial Services, Manufacturing, Retail, Telecommunications, High-Tech, Gaming), with a deep understanding of domestic procurement cycles and complex stakeholder navigation.

Own and execute the workplace services strategy across Bangalore, Mumbai and Delhi, ensuring our workplaces support business growth, operational excellence and an exceptional employee experience.

About the role

Every product Databricks ships has to be priced, contracted, rated and billed before it can earn a dollar. The Money organization builds the systems that make this happen, at hyperscaler scale and across every major cloud. We built the world's only cross-cloud integrated rating engine in-house, and it now rates billions of dollars in revenue. Our next goal is bigger: a fully automated, zero-touch order-to-cash flow where the platform is the source of truth for accounts, contracts and subscriptions, and Month End Close needs little or no human intervention.

As Director of Engineering, you will lead the engineering organization that owns this commercial engine from start to finish. You will set the product and technology strategy for how Databricks makes money. You will be the engineering voice Finance, Product and GTM leaders turn to for strategic decisions. You will also build the leadership bench that lets the organization keep scaling.

Speed is critical. Databricks keeps inventing new ways to sell: commit and pay-as-you-go, marketplaces, conditional benefits, strategic partnerships and new clouds and regions. The commerce engine either makes each of these fast and safe to launch, or it becomes the bottleneck. You will make sure it is the former.

What you'll own

The org covers six commercial domains:

Pricing configuration: SKUs, multipliers, price-change processes, deal desk and discounting

Orders and contracts: from negotiated quote to order to signed customer contract

Subscriptions: commit, pay-as-you-go and proof-of-concept subscriptions, plus how contracts are tied to payment methods

Rating: applying each customer's negotiated price, discounts and conditional benefits to ingested usage to compute the bill

Billing: commit drawdown, invoicing, Month End Close and related financial processes

Marketplace: third-party data and solutions, available seamlessly to Databricks customers

The impact you'll have

Set and communicate the vision. Write the multi-year product and technology strategy for the commerce engine, toward a zero-touch order-to-cash flow and a next-generation billing architecture. Present it clearly to executives, Finance and Product leaders, so that strategy and architecture decisions come to you by default.

Own business outcomes across orgs, not just your team's part. Revenue-critical programs routinely span 100+ people across Finance, Product, IT, Accounts and GTM. You will own the full outcome: dependency plans with clear owners, timelines, quality bars and escalation triggers, raised early in leadership forums so cross-org risks don't become executive surprises.

Make commercialization a platform capability. Build reusable building blocks (credits, commits, conditional benefits, marketplace and partner billing) so that new pricing models and routes to market ship in weeks, not quarters.

Treat foundations as seriously as features. Hold reliability, correctness, SOX and compliance readiness, security, cost visibility and operational load to the same standard as product launches. Billing errors should be structurally impossible, operational work should grow more slowly than revenue, and postmortems should actually lead to change.

Partner deeply with Business & Finance. Turn accounting, close and compliance requirements into engineering design. Keep improving the Month End Close timeline and audit readiness, and earn the trust of Technical Accounting, Revenue Ops and Strategy & Execution leaders.

Build a team of leaders. Grow the organization from one with a large group of direct-report engineers to one led by strong engineering managers and tech-lead managers, with clear subteams, domain boundaries and named owners. Coach managers to be great people leaders, give specific feedback and career plans, and recognize high-performing teams publicly.

Hire like a founder. Act as the hiring owner for the Money Bellevue site. Source and close senior engineering and management talent, put the company first when placing hires across Money teams, and help raise the Databricks engineering hiring bar.

What we're looking for

12+ years in software engineering, including 6+ years leading engineering organizations and managing managers, ideally in billing, payments, commerce, fintech or other systems where errors directly cost revenue or create regulatory exposure

A track record of delivering large, revenue-critical, cross-functional programs (for example, replacing a billing or rating system, migrating a source of truth, or automating order-to-cash) on time and with high quality

Technical depth in distributed systems and large-scale data pipelines. You can discuss correctness, idempotency, reconciliation and data lineage with tech leads, and you know when to coach and when to decide.

Fluency in order-to-cash and finance concepts: pricing and discounting, contracts, revenue recognition, invoicing, month-end close, SOX controls. You have earned trust as a partner to Finance and Accounting leaders.

Strong product judgment: you can spot gaps in the commercial platform, shape requirements with Product, and make build-versus-buy decisions that pay off over time

Clear, confident communication of strategy to executives, plus the ability to influence peers in Product, Finance, IT and GTM without direct authority

Experience scaling an organization quickly while keeping a high hiring bar, developing strong leaders and engineers, and keeping them engaged on internal platform work

BS in Computer Science or a related field; MS preferred. Experience with Kafka, Apache Spark, Delta Lake or cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP) is a plus.

You will run the engine behind the revenue of one of the fastest-growing data and AI companies in the world. The problems involve hard distributed-systems correctness at scale, high financial and compliance stakes, and a direct, visible link to company growth. You'll lead an established, high-trust team with a strong delivery record and help shape what the next generation of the commerce engine looks like.
